text:
Clara (CS): threading up a lightweight customer-facing runbook draft for prefill / caching / batching / streaming — goal: reduce renewal risk by improving first-24h UX and giving reps a simple script + telemetry hooks. Posting core bullets and examples here for quick review.
Diego (CS Ops): luv it. can we add a tiny decision tree for when to opt into prefill vs no-prefill? sales asks.
Noah (PM): yes — short decision points please (2-3 checks). also include suggested per-plan token budgets (ballpark) and a 0/24/72h check-in cadence.
Rina (Eng): adding runtime-safe defaults and a minimal API call to trigger a prefill. keep values conservative so we avoid over-provisioning.
Rina (Eng): config suggestion (copyable):
Rina (Eng): ```yaml
warmup:
  enabled: true
  window_minutes: 30
  concurrency_target: 3
cache:
  edge_ttl_seconds: 60
  local_kv_minutes: 15
batching:
  max_tokens_per_batch: 1024
  max_hold_ms: 25
streaming:
  prefer_stream: true
  streaming_grace_ms: 1200
fallback:
  use_cached_prefix: true
  degraded_max_tokens: 128
```
Taylor (SRE): add monitoring & probes: synthetic prefill probe every 3m hitting the same tenant path; alert if p95 > 350ms for 10m or error_rate > 1.5%. Also recommend a short oncall play when p95 spike coincides with increased prefill rate.
Clara (CS): customer-facing prefill blurb for kickoffs (short):
Clara (CS): "Hi <Customer>, to smooth your users' first interactions we run a short warmup when you go live. This briefly warms inference workers and caches recent examples for ~1h. It may generate a few internal preview calls — no action required. Reply if you prefer we skip."
Diego (CS Ops): ticketing change: add field `prefill_consent: yes/no` and `prefill_notes: <free text>` on onboarding ticket. rep should capture objections and cost concerns.
Noah (PM): renewal-risk signals to auto-escalate: (A) < 5 meaningful sessions in 48h AND (B) sustained p95 > 250ms for >12h -> create CS alert. If flagged twice within 7 days, auto-schedule a health call.
Rina (Eng): operational fallback: if streaming disconnects, runtime should immediately attempt cached-prefix streaming (if available) for up to 300ms, then switch to non-streaming single-shot with degraded_max_tokens. Keep a counter for fallback occurrences for postmortem.
Clara (CS): staging play for big demos / migrations: 1) trigger a 30m small warmup (concurrency_target 2) 2) ramp concurrency by ~1 every 10m to target 3) watch p95 and reduce batch hold if latency climbs.
Taylor (SRE): cost guardrails: when prefill total_tokens_estimate > plan_monthly_token_budget * 0.02, ops-bot should post a warning to the thread and set prefill throttling to soft (manual approval).
Diego (CS Ops): quick rep email template for handoff (short):
Diego (CS Ops): "Subject: Heads up — brief warmup before go-live\nHi <Name>, we plan a brief warmup to improve first-hour latency. It warms a small pool and caches sample prompts. Expect best performance immediately after. Reply if you'd like to opt-out.\nThanks, <rep>"
Clara (CS): sample consent checkbox language for the signup form: "I agree to a brief warmup (caching + warm pool) to improve initial latency (can opt-out)."
Noah (PM): per-plan token budget suggestions (very rough): Starter: 5M/mo, Growth: 50M/mo, Enterprise: 500M/mo. Recommend prefill default budget as 0.5% of monthly budget for first-24h and max 2% for first-week unless customer approves larger.
Rina (Eng): internal curl to trigger prefill (ops only):
Rina (Eng): ```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/tenants/T-001/prefill \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"steps":8,"sample_prompts":["onboard-welcome","faq"],"mode":"staggered"}'
```
enablement-bot: draft saved to Drive: https://drive.redwood/enablement/prefill-runbook-1762104321 (owner: Clara)
Taylor (SRE): ops checklist to add to runbook (one-liners):
Taylor (SRE): "- Confirm prefill_consent on ticket\n- Run synthetic prefill probe after warmup start\n- Observe p95 and errors for first 90m\n- If p95 > 500ms for >15m, pause additional warmup and notif CS\n- Record tokens used during warmup"
Clara (CS): next steps: I'll fold these into a 1-page runbook, add a tiny decision tree (opt-in criteria: high-interactive UX, <72h ramp, willing to accept small warmup token spend), and schedule a 15-min walk-through Thurs 9am PT. who can make it?
Diego (CS Ops): I can. will also bring updated ticket fields.
Noah (PM): I'll be there first 10.
Rina (Eng): can join to cover the curl/playbook bits last 5.
Clara (CS): great — thanks all. I'll post the one-pager link after the sync and tag SEs. :sparkles:
